 Property tax deadline extended due to late tax bills 
 Deb Hill
Reporter 
 Deb Hill 
 Reporter
 Author email 
 Nov 18, 2026 
 36 mins ago

 Fergus County Treasurer Kristy Taplin has arranged for a later than normal deadline for paying property taxes due to late arriving tax bills.
 Courtesy Photo
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 Save 
 Fergus County property tax bills went out a bit late this year, due to a glitch in calculating some fire district mill rates, so the payment deadline has been extended to Dec. 10.
 Fergus County property owners began receiving their tax bills this past weekend, just two weeks before the traditional payment deadline of Nov. 30.
 “We’re not sure exactly what happened, but the mills calulated for some of the fire districts appeared to be fine on our end. But when the tax bills reached the printer, the mills were distributed incorrectly. We had to fix those and resend the bills to the printer, which meant they went out later than normal,” said Fergus County Treasurer Kristy Klakken-Taplin.
 Taplin said she knew the short notice could make it difficult for people to pay their property tax bills on time, so she arranged for the payment deadline to be extended to Dec. 10.
 “I understand the delay in receiving the tax bills is frustrating,” Taplin said. “I apologize for the late notice, and really appreciate everyone’s understanding in this.”
 Taplin said it’s unclear what caused the glitch, but it was caught before the bills were mailed to taxpayers. The corrected information was provided to the printer. Property owners should be receiving their bills soon.
 “Probably about 40 people have called our office, wondering why they hadn’t yet received their property tax bill,” Taplin said. “If you haven’t received yours, it should arrive soon.”
 While property taxes now are due Dec. 10, mobile home taxes are still due Nov. 30, Taplin said.
 Payments can be sent by mail to the Fergus County Treasurer’s office, paid in person at the office on the second floor of the courthouse or paid online at https://itax.tylertech.com/fergusmt .
 Taplin reminded property owners who did not sign up for the Homestead exclusion last year, and whose tax bills include a hefty increase as a result, that they may be eligible for a refund starting Jan. 1.
 “If you didn’t submit your property information to claim the Homestead Reduced Tax Rate, you can go online and sign up now,” Taplin said.
 Those who qualify, meaning the property is their primary residence and they lived there for at least seven months in 2026, can get a refund for the difference between what they paid in property tax and what they would have paid if they had registered for the Homestead Reduced Tax Rate.
 For more information on the refund and which properties qualify, visit the Montana Department of Revenue website https://revenue.mt.gov/property/property-tax-changes/refund/ .
 Taplin reminds tax payers that property tax payments must be submitted by the due dates (Nov. 30 for mobile home taxes and Dec. 10 for real estate taxes) in order to avoid penalties and interest charges.
 For more information, contact the Fergus County Treasurer’s office at (406) 535-9220.
